title: The National Design Studio Became a DOGE Landing Pad. Now ‘Big Balls’ Is Recruiting
gist: The National Design Studio, headed by Airbnb cofounder Joe Gebbia as US chief design officer and nested under the Executive Office of the President, has absorbed former DOGE operatives including Edward 'Big Balls' Coristine, now its head of engineering. An engineer who was cold-pitched by Coristine describes an interview with no recruiter, no visible process and an interviewer who appeared unable to evaluate a full-stack engineer, for a role supporting Rampart — a browser PII-blocking tool the engineer calls counterintuitive for government services that require PII — while NDS hires outside USAJobs and has drawn Privacy Act scrutiny over sites collecting passport and voter registration data.

insights.claim: The first iteration of DOGE began winding down with Elon Musk's departure from government in June 2025, and the National Design Studio emerged much more quietly less than two months later under another tech billionaire.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Institutional continuity under a rebranded, lower-profile entity means the DOGE model persists past its founder's exit — watch NDS rather than DOGE for where this operating style shows up next.
insights.locator: Last year, the first iteration of the so-called Department of Government Efficiency

insights.claim: The National Design Studio is headed by Airbnb cofounder Joe Gebbia, who serves as the country's chief design officer, with a stated mission of redesigning government websites to be beautifully designed with a great user experience.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Consumer-product design leadership placed over federal digital services is a template other administrations and governments may copy or react against.
insights.locator: NDS is headed by Joe Gebbia, the cofounder of Airbnb

insights.claim: NDS retains many hallmarks of DOGE including some of its team members, an opaque structure and a seeming lack of adherence to the way many federal rules and systems work, and like DOGE it is nested under the Executive Office of the President.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Placement under the EOP is what enables the process deviations — the structural feature to watch when assessing legal exposure of these units.
insights.locator: But NDS retains many of the hallmarks of DOGE

insights.claim: Edward 'Big Balls' Coristine — 19 years old when he joined the government and reportedly terminated from a network-monitoring-firm internship after being suspected of leaking internal information — is now the National Design Studio's head of engineering, alongside fellow early DOGE engineer Akash Bobba.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Personnel continuity is the concrete mechanism by which DOGE's approach survives; the same names reappearing is the trackable signal.
insights.locator: Gebbia has long been a close associate of Musk’s

insights.claim: NDS membership is ambiguous: HHS chief technology officer and former DOGE affiliate Zachary Terrell 'contributes' to NDS per his own website, and Akash Bobba retained an unpaid expert appointment at OPM until March 7, 2026 — more than six months after reportedly moving to NDS — per documents in an American Federation of Government Employees lawsuit.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Overlapping unpaid and cross-agency appointments blur accountability lines and are exactly what union litigation is targeting — a live legal risk to the arrangement.
insights.locator: It’s not always clear who is a part of NDS

insights.claim: White House spokesperson Davis Ingle defended the unit, saying NDS under Gebbia is doing outstanding work modernizing federal digital and physical services and that Trump has consistently prioritized innovation and efficiency, while NDS, HHS and OPM did not reply to requests for comment.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The only on-record institutional defense comes from the White House press office rather than the agencies involved — a measure of how thin the accountability surface is.
insights.quote: The National Design Studio, under the leadership of Joe Gebbia, is doing outstanding work modernizing federal digital and physical services
insights.locator: “The National Design Studio, under the leadership of Joe Gebbia

insights.claim: NDS says on its website that it is hiring but provides little role information and seemingly no way to apply, and its jobs do not appear on USAJobs, the federal hiring portal — mirroring DOGE, which solicited applications through a separate website and via direct message on X before the January 2025 inauguration.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Recruiting outside the statutory federal hiring channel is both the efficiency claim and the legal vulnerability — a recurring pattern in these units.
insights.locator: Though the NDS website says that the group is hiring

insights.claim: An engineer who had not applied received a cold pitch from Coristine that framed NDS's work as creating agentic experiences where Americans can get things done with their government and sought very talented and hardcore engineers who can ship.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The stated product direction — agentic citizen-facing government services — is a concrete signal of where federal AI deployment is heading and which vendors it may bypass.
insights.quote: We’re taking the leap to create agentic experiences where Americans can get things done with their government
insights.locator: Instead, they received a cold pitch from Coristine

insights.claim: The interviewing engineer, who has previously worked in government, said the process departed from federal norms: no recruiter was present, only Coristine was on a video call rather than the standard bias-reducing phone screen, and the candidate had no idea how NDS obtained their contact information.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Abandonment of structured screening is where merit-hiring litigation and IG scrutiny typically start.
insights.quote: Normally initial screenings are done over the phone, rather than video, to reduce bias in the process
insights.locator: I have no idea how they got my contact information

insights.claim: The candidate said the interview was casual to the point that no process appeared to be established, and that Coristine did not seem aware of the skill sets and tools needed to evaluate a full-stack engineer.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Technical evaluation capacity at the top of the org determines build quality — a leading indicator of whether NDS ships anything durable.
insights.quote: But it was casual to the point where I don't think there was any process established.
insights.locator: “I don't want to come off as a prude

insights.claim: In January 2025 Coristine was among DOGE members who interviewed General Services Administration Technology Transformation Services workers required to defend their jobs and projects, in meetings employees described as showing the DOGE members were not familiar with their work.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The same evaluation-capacity gap that shaped DOGE's staff cuts is now shaping NDS's hires — the pattern repeats with the same individuals.

themes.theme: Rampart and the product logic problem

insights.claim: The role Coristine pitched supports Rampart, a tool released in late June to prevent personally identifiable information from leaving a user's browser, particularly when using something like a chatbot.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Client-side PII redaction for chatbot use is a specific, buildable category — its appearance inside government signals expected chatbot deployment across citizen services.
insights.locator: Coristine told the engineer that the role was geared toward supporting

insights.claim: Coristine described Rampart as a 'side quest' on the TBPN podcast and told the engineer that the roughly 30-person NDS team did not include a machine-learning engineer.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: A 30-person unit with no ML engineer building AI-adjacent privacy tooling sets a low ceiling on what it can actually deliver.
insights.locator: In an interview with the Technology Business Programming Network (TBPN) podcast

insights.claim: Rampart resembles OpenAI's browser-based privacy filter that detects and masks personal emails, addresses or account numbers, but is significantly smaller, which Coristine argues makes it more accessible in lower-bandwidth environments.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: A government unit rebuilding a capability a frontier lab already ships raises the question of build-versus-adopt for public-sector AI tooling generally.
insights.locator: The tool is similar to OpenAI’s browser-based “privacy filter,”

insights.claim: The engineer argues Rampart is counterintuitive for government use because accessing benefits typically requires the user to supply PII such as a social security number or address, and that field-level encryption plus HTTPS already protect data in transit.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: If the flagship tool solves a problem that does not exist in its own domain, NDS's output has little practical value regardless of design quality.
insights.quote: It feels very counterintuitive because in most instances, when you are asking for PII, you want PII

insights.claim: The engineer's most optimistic reading is that NDS is an organization with no goals, noting that NIST regularly supports the creation of tools for complex privacy and technical problems, and asks why people so closely associated with the White House are spending tax money on what they call a little hacker project.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Duplicating existing federal technical institutions is the specific inefficiency critique that makes efficiency-branded units politically vulnerable.
insights.quote: Why are these guys who are so closely associated with the White House wasting tax money on this little hacker project?
insights.locator: “This does feel superfluous

themes.theme: Privacy exposure and prior destruction of capacity

insights.claim: The Guardian reported in June that NDS appeared to be building government websites where users enter sensitive information including for passports and voter registration, and that already-deployed NDS sites used commercial tracking tools that did not appear to comply with the Privacy Act.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Commercial analytics on federal sites collecting identity data is a concrete Privacy Act liability and a likely trigger for litigation or congressional inquiry.
insights.locator: Though NDS members don’t seem to be getting access

insights.claim: Voter registration is handled by the states and the passport application website has historically been run by the State Department rather than the White House, making NDS's involvement a jurisdictional departure.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: White House-run interfaces to state election functions and State Department services is the kind of jurisdictional shift that attracts federalism litigation.
insights.locator: Voter registration is handled by the states

insights.claim: In a conversation with the National Association of Secretaries of State about the voter registration website, Akash Bobba reportedly told attendees he did not know what data was retained or logged.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
entities: National Association of Secretaries of State
insights.so_what: An operator unable to describe data retention on an election-adjacent system is the single most quotable governance failure in the piece.
insights.quote: I don’t know what they retain and what they are logging.
insights.locator: In a conversation with the National Association of Secretaries of State

insights.claim: DOGE previously fired technologists already working on the kinds of projects it claimed to want and killed the Internal Revenue Service's free tax filing tool, while an OPM memo published last week instructed agencies to prioritize hiring technical talent.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Capacity destroyed and then re-hired at a premium is the measurable cost of the efficiency program — the pattern to price when evaluating similar reorganizations.
insights.locator: This is not the first time the Trump administration has tried to reinvent the wheel
